title: String.to_float() counts leading zeros against its 18-digit limit: "00000000000000000001.5" parses as 0
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable (4.7.2.stable.arch_linux.ed1daf0bf)
- Not a regression: the same `built_in_strtod()` digit-counting code (`if (mantSize > 18)`) is present in the 1.0-stable, 3.6-stable, 4.0-stable and 4.6-stable sources and is unchanged on master, so the bug has likely existed since Godot 1.0.

### System information

Linux - Arch - Godot 4.7.2 stable

### Issue description

Tested versions: Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable. The parser is unchanged on master.

System information: Godot v4.7.2.stable.arch_linux (ed1daf0bf) - Arch Linux - Linux 7.2.6-arch2-1 (x86_64). This is core string parsing, so it doesn't depend on the platform.

Issue description:
`String.to_float()` reads at most 18 digit characters, and leading zeros count toward that limit. The same parser is used by `float(String)`, `str_to_var()`, `JSON.parse_string()` and GDScript float literals. Fixed-point numbers with many leading zeros get truncated or read as 0, even though they pass `is_valid_float()`:

| input | result | expected |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `"00000000000000000001.5"` | `0` | `1.5` |
| `"0.0000000000000000271"` | `2e-17` | `2.71e-17` |
| `"271e-19"` | `2.71e-17` | `2.71e-17` |

**Cause:** [`built_in_strtod()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/core/string/ustring.cpp#L2445-L2505) counts every digit, leading zeros included, caps the count at 18, and reads the first 18 digits. Significant digits past that point are dropped. Skipping leading zeros before counting would fix it.

**Related, lower priority:** the parser is also not correctly rounded. About 1 in 6 of the shortest decimals printed by `String.num_scientific()` read back 1 ulp off, so `float(String.num_scientific(v)) == v` fails for some `v`. For example, `"1.8143934130161599"` reads as `1.81439341301616`. `"1e-320"` reads as `0` because 10^320 overflows before the divide. A correctly rounded, locale-independent parser such as [fast_float](https://github.com/fastfloat/fast_float) would fix both.

Steps to reproduce: godot --headless --script repro.gd
```gdscript
extends SceneTree

func _init() -> void:
      for s in ["00000000000000000001.5", "0.0000000000000000271", "271e-19", "1.8143934130161599", "1e-320"]:
              print("%-24s -> %s" % [s, String.num_scientific(float(s))])
      quit()
```
Steps to reproduce: godot --headless --script repro.gd
```gdscript
extends SceneTree

func _init() -> void:
      for s in ["00000000000000000001.5", "0.0000000000000000271", "271e-19", "1.8143934130161599", "1e-320"]:
              print("%-24s -> %s" % [s, String.num_scientific(float(s))])
      quit()
```

Minimal reproduction project: The script above is self-contained, so no project is needed.

I trimmed the repro to five inputs. It's the same code as before, but I haven't re-run this shorter version. The expected output is 0, 2e-17, 2.71e-17, 1.81439341301616 and 0.
